overview.mechanism: A polyclonal antibody preparation targeting lymphocytes; source species and manufacturing determine the specific preparation.
uses: Immunosuppressive treatment in product-specific indications. This Philippine registry entry specifies equine ATG.

paragraphs.text: Equine and rabbit ATG are not interchangeable dose-for-dose. A randomized trial in severe acquired aplastic anemia found different response and survival outcomes for horse and rabbit preparations; those results apply to that clinical setting.

The US equine ATG reference label includes serious hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis precautions and specialist infusion monitoring. It is linked as an equine reference, not as proof that the Philippine Thymogam product has identical dosing or all the same indications.

The US ATGAM label contraindicates treatment after prior anaphylaxis to ATGAM or another equine gamma globulin. It strongly recommends pretreatment skin testing, but a negative test does not exclude anaphylaxis and does not predict serum sickness.

ATGAM is infused over at least four hours in a facility equipped to treat anaphylaxis, with observation during infusion and for at least 24 hours afterward. These instructions describe the US reference product; the Philippine equine preparation requires its own insert.

Monitor for cytokine release, infusion reactions, delayed serum sickness and opportunistic infection or viral reactivation. Severe persistent thrombocytopenia or neutropenia may require discontinuation. The label calls for clinically indicated liver and kidney tests and avoidance of live vaccines around treatment.

sources.citation: Scheinberg et al. Horse versus rabbit antithymocyte globulin in acquired aplastic anemia. N Engl J Med. 2011;365:430–438. PubMed PMID: 21812672.
ATGAM (equine anti-thymocyte globulin) US prescribing information. DailyMed. Reference product; Philippine labeling may differ.
